sentences.text: In dimension omega, the categories of omega-categorial algebras, in both presentations, are projective limits of their finite truncations:
an omega-dimensional algebra is the same as a compatible family of finite ones.
Truncation and discretization to and from omega are still induced by generalized H E P derivors, and graduation follows from the universal property of the limit.
But the two presentations now behave differently.
When there is at least one sort, the homogeneous omega-categorial algebras are not defined by Q E equations, because a product of cells of ever higher dimension has no finite dimension.
